title: BEST Commands
description: Schema for the command ingestion and discovery capability (io.best.agents.commands).

command.description: A command sent to a BEST-compliant service. CloudEvent 1.0 envelope — the type field must match a type in the command catalogue, and the data property is validated against the JSON Schema at the dataschema URI before the command is queued. dataschema is required for commands.

commandCatalogueEntry.description: An entry in the command catalogue — one available command type with its schema name, version, and dataschema URI.

schema.description: Command schema name in kebab-case (e.g. propose-counter, submit-order). Used as the {schema} path segment in GET /commands/{schema}/{version}. Distinct from the CloudEvent 'type' field.

version.description: Schema version string (e.g. 1.0, 2.1). Used as the {version} path segment in GET /commands/{schema}/{version}. First-class field — callers do not need to parse the dataschema URI to determine the version.

dataschema.description: Resolvable URI to the JSON Schema for this command's data payload. Canonical value for the dataschema field of a CloudEvent command. Kept for CloudEvent compatibility.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this command does.

workflows.description: Ids of published workflows (io.best.agents.workflows) this command participates in — the protocol's single workflow-discoverability mechanism, stamped both here and as a top-level member of the command's schema document. Servers SHOULD populate it for every operation that appears in a recipe; consumers SHOULD read the recipe before composing a multi-step sequence themselves.

impact.description: High-impact annotation — declares that this command is high-impact in the sense of the Security Requirements (destructive, irreversible, financial, or compliance-relevant) and that a consumer acting on behalf of a human must warn that human and obtain explicit confirmation before submitting it. Stamped both on the catalogue entry and as a top-level member of the command's schema document; both surfaces MUST carry the same value. Descriptive only: it never replaces the server-side controls the Security Requirements demand for high-impact commands.

categories.description: What kind of impact the command has. Named values: 'financial' (moves money or puts capital at risk), 'destructive' (removes data or state), 'irreversible' (cannot be undone by a compensating command), 'compliance' (bypasses or alters a compliance control). The vocabulary is open — implementers MAY add their own values; consumers treat unknown values as high-impact.

confirmation.description: 'required': a consumer acting on behalf of a human MUST NOT submit this command without explicit, per-submission confirmation from that human. 'recommended': the consumer SHOULD confirm but MAY proceed when the human has durably authorized this class of operation. Service-to-service automation with no human principal is governed by the server-side High-impact controls instead.

warning.description: Human-readable warning the consumer SHOULD surface to the human, substantially intact, before asking for confirmation (e.g. 'Places a real order on your broker account. Capital at risk.').

commandCatalogue.description: Response body for GET /commands. Lists all command types this service accepts, with their schema URIs. This is the discovery surface for callers (Process Managers, AI agents, UIs) to learn what they can send.

schemaEntry.description: An entry describing one available command schema with its version. Returned in the command catalogue entry's dataschema URI path.

schema.description: Schema name (e.g. ProposeCounter, SubmitOrder). Matches the command type name.

version.description: Schema version string (e.g. 1.0, 2.1). Used as the second path segment in GET /commands/{schema}/{version}.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this schema validates.
